seats.name: seat-1
argv:
Read spec.txt (the STAMP language) and program.stamp. Determine exactly what the program outputs
when run under that specification.

Write your final answer, and only your final answer with no explanation, to a file named
answer.txt in your current working directory: the printed values in order, separated by single
spaces, on one line.

The room's final agreed proposal text must be exactly your answer and nothing else (no explanation) — that text is read as the submitted answer once the room concludes.

Join room rq1 as seat-1 (agent claude, expected_participants 3). Leave the room once it has concluded.
seats.text:
The room reached consensus 3/3 on the program's output, and I've written it to `answer.txt`:

`105 100 101 101 102 101 2432902008176640000 0 7 101 7 7 7 3 15 0 0 4 6 30 0 27 10 23 1 1 3 1267650600228229401496703205376 1 0 0 -3 100 5`

I did this by tracing the program by hand against the spec, not by running an interpreter. The only commands I ran were a check of the two big values (2^100 and 20!) and a word count of `answer.txt`. All three seats' traces agree on the final text. seat-3's opening left out the second 101 after 102, and their proposal added it back. I've left the room.

seats.text:
The room concluded 3/3 on the answer below, and I've left it. I wrote the same line to `answer.txt`.

```
105 100 101 101 102 101 2432902008176640000 0 7 101 7 7 7 3 15 0 0 4 6 30 0 27 10 23 1 1 3 1267650600228229401496703205376 1 0 0 -3 100 5
```

I got this by tracing `program.stamp` by hand against `spec.txt`; I didn't run an interpreter. The other two seats' traces matched mine. Seat-3's opening answer had left out the second `101`. That was the `PRINT total` after `tick`, whose `NEXT` makes a local, so the global stays 101. Seat-3's proposal already had it fixed.

The accepted proposal is exactly this line with no explanation.

seats.text:
The room concluded 3/3 on the proposal, and I've left it. `answer.txt` in the workspace holds the agreed output, on one line:

`105 100 101 101 102 101 2432902008176640000 0 7 101 7 7 7 3 15 0 0 4 6 30 0 27 10 23 1 1 3 1267650600228229401496703205376 1 0 0 -3 100 5`

I worked this out by tracing the program by hand against the spec. I never ran it through an interpreter, and the two other seats each traced it independently to the same values.
